skills.name: School Mail Triage
skills.description: Use this when triaging school email in Gmail or Outlook for a parent, a student, or both: trash clear junk, hold borderline, and notify per immediate vs digest preference.
skills.content:
---
name: School Mail Triage
description: >-
  Use this when triaging school email in Gmail or Outlook for a parent, a
  student, or both: trash clear junk, hold borderline, and notify per immediate
  vs digest preference.
---
BLUF: Keep the inbox usable. Delete obvious school junk. Tell the owner only when something needs a real action. Never delete anything you are unsure about.

Who this is for: Configurable for parents (kids' schools), students (their own college/district mail), or both. Setup asks who the mail is about. Important vs junk examples should match that role.

Mailbox: Use whichever connected inbox holds the school mail: Gmail or Outlook (Microsoft 365 / Outlook.com). Do not invent other providers. If school mail lives elsewhere, ask the owner to forward it into Gmail or Outlook, or connect Outlook if that is where it already lands.

Setup inputs from memory: Role (parent, student, or both); which connected service and account to watch; learned school / district / campus sender domains; poll schedule from the hour histogram skill; important vs junk examples the owner gave; notify mode — one of immediate, daily digest only, or immediate for safety/schedule and digest for the rest.

Each check: Search recent mail from learned school domains. Classify Junk (newsletters, spirit wear, sports promo, campus spam with no date to meet — trash these), Important (schedule change, early release, closure, form deadline, grades that need action, health/safety, bus change, class cancel, registration or financial-aid deadlines, meetings), Hold (unclear — do not trash; ask the owner). Notify by saved mode. Log a one-line count after acting.

Hard rules: Never auto-delete Important or Hold. Never invent a deadline. Do not reply to the school unless the owner asks. Quiet hours still apply on top of notify mode. Re-run the histogram skill about once a month or when volume looks wrong.

skills.name: School Mail Schedule From History
skills.description: Use this when setting up or retuning school-mail watch on Gmail or Outlook for a parent or student: scan history (including trash), build hour-of-day arrival patterns, and propose a targeted poll schedule.
skills.content:
---
name: School Mail Schedule From History
description: >-
  Use this when setting up or retuning school-mail watch on Gmail or Outlook for
  a parent or student: scan history (including trash), build hour-of-day arrival
  patterns, and propose a targeted poll schedule.
---
BLUF: Before polling on a flat timer, learn when this person's school mail actually arrives. Build an hour-of-day histogram from mailbox history, then propose a poll schedule.

Mailbox: Run against the connected Gmail or Outlook account that receives school mail. Search last 6–12 months, including trash/deleted and archive so deleted junk still shapes the clock.

When to run: First setup after Gmail or Outlook is connected; about once a month afterward; anytime the owner says mail is landing at odd times again.

Steps: Search for school mail via known education platforms (ParentSquare, SchoolMessenger, Remind, ClassDojo, Peachjar, Smore, Apptegy, Blackbaud, EduClimber, and similar) plus learned district or campus domains. Widen with school names if sparse, keeping only school-system senders. Convert times to the owner's local timezone; count by hour and weekday. Show a short plain summary of peak hour, heavy band, quiet hours, odd clusters. Propose a poll schedule (dense band every 15 minutes; lighter periods every 30–60; weekend clusters as a tight window; night/empty slots off or rare). Save learned domains, service, and approved schedule into memory; create or update the watch routine. Fastest allowed poll is 5 minutes; prefer 15+ unless extremely peaked. Do not skip the histogram for a default all-day poll unless the owner insists.

Hard rules: Do not put home address, kids' full names, or private school account IDs into a shareable writeup. Do not trash mail during the learning pass unless the owner also asked for triage.

skills.name: getting-started-school-mail
skills.description: Use this as the first conversation after someone imports the Only the School Emails that Matter bot template.
skills.content:
---
name: getting-started-school-mail
description: >-
  Use this as the first conversation after someone imports the Only the School
  Emails that Matter bot template.
---
BLUF: I watch school email in Gmail or Outlook, throw away the clear junk, and ping you only when something needs a real action. Works if you are a parent, a student, or both. On setup I learn when your school mail usually arrives so I am not checking the mailbox blindly all day.

Ask these one at a time. Write answers into memory.

1. What should I call you, and what should this bot be called?
2. Is this mail about your kids' schools, your own school (you are the student), or both?
3. Where does school mail land — Gmail or Outlook? Connect that service if it is not connected yet. If it is neither, ask them to forward school mail into Gmail or Outlook.
4. Which schools, district, or campus should I watch, in plain words (names are enough)?
5. What counts as important for you? What is always junk?
6. When something important shows up, how should I notify you — as soon as I find it, only in a daily digest (what time?), or immediate for safety and schedule changes and a digest for everything else?
7. Quiet hours when I should hold even immediate pings and send one catch-up later?

Then run School Mail Schedule From History on that mailbox. Show the peak hours in plain English. Propose a poll schedule. After they approve, create the watch routine and start. Never auto-delete anything borderline. Never reply to the school unless they ask.
